title: I Love How Music Makes Soulframe Feel Like A Folktale
description: Soulframe still isn't out yet, but its Preludes were finally publicly opened on November 6, giving me my first chance to try it out. I was expecting " Warframe but fantasy," and to be fair, a lot of Soulframe is like that, but so much of Digital Extremes' new action-role-playing game feels very different. I'm floored--I've tried to get into Warframe several times and just kept bouncing off of it for one reason or another, but here I am really enjoying Soulframe and trying to figure out which live-service game I'm going to have to retire from to put Soulframe into my regular rotation. And it's really all because of the game's music. Admittedly, music is one of the best parts about Warframe too. While I've never been able to really get into it, the reason I kept trying Warframe is because I'd keep hearing these absolute awesome sea shanties and vocal-led orchestral scores and thinking, "I want to play a game that sounds like that." But I never knew how to get to any of those moments to hear them play out in game. I tried getting into Warframe way too late, when the game had already transformed into something that largely catered to the players who were already in the ecosystem. The game just felt way too big of a beast to tackle as a newbie. Which is fine! That happens to every live-service game eventually. Soulframe is new so it doesn't have that problem yet. And even if it did, it feels like it incorporates its music way more regularly and meaningfully than Warframe seems to. Almost every aspect of Soulframe (so far) is shaped around its music, including its poetry, birdsong, choral folktales, and orchestral scores. Character creation is writing a poem about how beautiful your mother was, several characters communicate solely in sing-song rhyme, and the first storyline revolves around learning the song that will not only play during the climatic boss battle but will also be played by your character in order to finally cleanse the evil you're fighting. In Soulframe,…

title: “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight. As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse. In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6. At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response. If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion
description: Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says. Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company." He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it. "We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said. Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops. "But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed." In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid. In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid. Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead, so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster, and that could be a positive for the company's financials. GTA 6…

title: GTA 6 Could Sell 55 Million Copies By Early Next Year, Report Says, And Average Selling Price Could Be $90
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how big will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut. In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled. "This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league." GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50. Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online. Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well. Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026, and currently trades around $228/share.. A new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and…

title: You Can Probably Guess WoW: Forever’s Most Popular Race, Class, And Faction
description: World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG. Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular. For that, we turn to Raider.IO, a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression. A snapshot of WoW: Forever stats after one week. According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde. The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde. It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo. Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that. As for what rulesets are…

title: Magic: The Gathering Planeswalker Hits Netflix In 2027, Watch The Trailer Now
description: MagicCon: Atlanta has kicked off with The Preview Panel, which usually shows off cards from future sets. While Nauctis: The Sunken Realm did feature during the panel, Wizards of the Coast then gave the Atlanta crowd more information on Planeswalker, the upcoming animated series set in the Magic multiverse, which is coming to Netflix in 2027. The two-minute teaser highlighted the animation team at Hungary-based Digic Pictures, along with showrunner Terry Matalas, Magic head of story Roy Graham, and more. A few brief moments of Chandra and Ajani were mixed in with the behind-the-scenes footage, offering a first look at the upcoming show's animation style. Planeswalker's official description reveals that the show will follow Chandra, MTG's pyromancer planeswalker. She and other planeswalkers like Ajani must "harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence," according to the Netflix Tudum blog post. A TV series for Magic: The Gathering is a long time coming, as the card game and its story have been going for over 30 years. There's a lot of fertile ground within the Magic multiverse, and as Chandra has been a key part of that story for nearly half that time, we're curious how many of Magic's worlds will be featured in Planeswalker. The Preview Panel at MagicCon: Atlanta also revealed multiple cards from Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, as well as the next Untold Stories series from comic publisher Dark Horse--which will also follow Chandra--and a new novel set in the cyberpunk world of Kamigawa. Planeswalker is set to launch on Netflix in 2027, though no specific dates have been revealed as of this writing.

title: Super Mario 3D Land Dared To Embrace 2D Mario In A 3D World
description: Super Mario 3D Land is celebrating its 15-year anniversary today, November 13, 2026. Below, we examine how 3D Land was a true iteration of the classic 2D Mario formula. I remember when the first preview images of Super Mario 64 began circulating in gaming magazines. The thought of playing a Mario game in THREE DEEEEEE blew my tiny 8-year-old mind. While the final game was absolutely wonderful, it wasn’t quite what I had in my head when I thought about Mario gameplay translated into three dimensions. The worlds were vast and open-ended. Instead of running and jumping toward the goal, players had missions to accomplish. Puzzles to solve. Specific enemies to beat. Trinkets to find. Mario had a life bar. An air meter when underwater. Power-ups were temporary, vanishing after a certain time had elapsed. And don’t get me wrong. It was different from what I imagined, but it worked. All of it worked. Nintendo had a winning formula on its hands, one that 3D Mario games would carry forward with Super Mario Sunshine and, to a lesser extent, the Super Mario Galaxy duology. But deep down, I couldn’t help but wonder what it would have been like in some alternate universe where they had adhered to the classic Mario formula instead in the move to 3D. Super Mario 3D Land Thankfully, I didn’t have to wonder forever, because in 2011, Super Mario 3D Land released for the 3DS and changed what a 3D Mario game could be. How? By doing exactly what I wanted Super Mario 64 to do 15 years prior: fully translate the classic 2D Mario style and gameplay to the third dimension. Even looking at 3D Land’s cover art evokes memories of the plumber’s colorful side-scrolling escapades. We see Mario hopping around a colorful environment full to the brim with blocks, pipes, platforms, even classic power-ups like the Fire Flower tucked away in the corner. And few elements could get the nostalgia juices flowing like the inclusion of the iconic Super Leaf from Super Mario Bros. 3. The game promised to be…

title: After A Week With WoW: Forever, Classic WoW Feels New Again
description: It's been just over a week since the record-breaking launch of World of Warcraft: Forever. In that time a handful of players have raced to level 60, but the overwhelming majority are still weeks away from reaching max level, as they quest through Azeroth and see all the new sights and sounds Blizzard has cooked up. So far, it's been (mostly) an absolute joy. I've spent every spare moment I can find in developer Blizzard's millennial retirement home, and after one week, it's safe to say I'm more than a little consumed by it. I was already a lover of original WoW, having grown up playing it, and have since spent thousands of hours playing WoW Classic after it launched in 2019. Having a new version of this MMORPG, one that's still unexplored and filled with new sights and sounds, is in many ways a dream come true. That's not to say it's all sunshine and rainbows in Stormwind (or, if you prefer, Orgrimmar). Forever certainly has a lot going for it, and its launch was quite possibly the smoothest in Blizzard's entire history. That being said, while Forever is nearly everything I could want from a "Classic Plus" experience, I do have a few gripes I hope Blizzard takes a closer look at in the weeks and months to come. Here's what's working, what I'm most impressed by, and what I'm still on the fence about as we enter the second week of Forever. Good - The World Is Alive MMO launches are special occasions. It's when the game is likely to be the most populated it will ever be, and at any given moment you can see dozens of players running down the road, flooding questing areas, or hawking their wares in a capital city. Forever's launch was no exception, and it was, in a word, magical. Players were everywhere, and it made Azeroth feel alive again in a way that hasn't been seen since WoW Classic Season of Discovery. Massive crowds have been an issue in past WoW Classic launches, as everyone competes to tag enemies they need for quests or loot specific items, but I found it to…

title: Official Zelda Website Raises Eyebrows By Labeling 3DS Game As Playable On Switch
description: Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game. A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site. Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter. Nintendo's official website briefly listed A Link Between Worlds as a playable game through NSO. The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time ( the original ), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap. If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service. Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

title: GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Says
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2, an outlier at $80? According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples. A scene from GTA 6. Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices. However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said. "The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added. Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports…

title: Friday The 13th Is Finally Returning To Movies, But Are Games Next?
description: Everyone's favorite hockey-mask-wearing killer is finally set to return to the big screen for the first time in almost two decades, with a new film starring him set for release in 2027. Per Deadline, veteran Friday the 13th director Steve Miner--who directed Friday the 13th: Part 2, Part 3, and the Halloween H20: 20 Years Later film that featured Jason's mask-wearing rival, Michael Myers--will helm this project. The Friday the 13th franchise has been largely absent from cinema, as a grueling battle over the franchise rights played out for years between screenwriter Victor Miller and production companies Horror, Inc. and the Manny Company (backed by original producer Sean S. Cunningham). Fast-forward to 2026, and things have been settled. Miller has ownership of elements introduced in his original Friday the 13th screenplay--including Camp Crystal Lake, Pamela Voorhees, and the child version of Jason--while Cunningham's company retains foreign distribution rights to the original film, ownership of all sequels, and the trademark on the adult version of Jason Voorhees, who was introduced in later installments. Because neither side can use the full Friday the 13th mythology alone, both camps came together with the film studio A24, which acts as a neutral bridge between them. Both sides receive executive producer credits on Jason projects, and this also saw the launch of the Jason Universe to foster broader franchise cooperation. Thanks to that new sense of collaboration, we got the Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, which has proven to be something of a critical hit. For film fans, this will be the first Jason movie since the 2009 reboot, which arrived as Hollywood's obsession with remaking horror movies was winding down. While that was the last we'd see of Jason and his machete on the silver screen for many years, the character lived on in the fun video game adaptation first released in 2017.
